links.outcome: Distribution of ophthalmic access by patient subgroup between AI and standard-of-care referral pathways
links.effect: AI referral pathway patients were more likely to be Black (p < 0.001) and have hypertension (p = 0.001); no difference in presenting BCVA between pathways.
links.quote: However, patients from the AI referral pathway were more likely to be Black (p < 0.001) and have hypertension (p = 0.001), suggesting that deployment of autonomous AI is associated with improved ophthalmic access for patients with a higher baseline risk for poor DED outcome before vision loss has occurred.

unlisted_practices: Autonomous AI diabetic eye exam at primary care to improve referral access to ophthalmology

screen.reason: Evaluates the real-world deployment of autonomous AI for diabetic eye disease screening in primary care and its impact on ophthalmic access across patient subgroups, but does not compare specific deployment practices/safeguards.
